nonblocking_findings: CLOSED, formerly blocking (expanded-309.png, printed p.307, unexplained rule near the top of the page): the evidence closes this. On expanded-308.png (printed p.306) the page ends with the announced optional addition: the bold rubric 'ויש מוסיפים:' and then 'היום תתמכנו בימין צדקך: אמן:'. There is no rule before it, which matches the proof's statement that the rubric announces the opening. The TeX fragment in layout-context-proof.json shows \OSCondEndBlock{} in the same \pstart as the 'סוגרים הארון.' instruction note, right after the היום תתמכנו paragraph. The XML context shows the matching j:conditional and j:endConditional around exactly that paragraph. On 309 the rule sits directly above 'סוגרים הארון.', in the position that fragment predicts. It is a deliberate conditional-scope end marker, not a footnote rule or a stray orphan. Footnote 138 on 311 uses a separate rule at the bottom of the page, so the two can't be mixed up.

NEW, cosmetic (308→309): the optional addition's content is on p.306 but its closing scope rule lands at the top of p.307, after the page break. The opening has no matching rule, so a reader who meets the lone rule at the top of 307 has to turn back a page to see what it closes. Keeping the end marker on the same page as the conditional content (for example with a no-break penalty before \OSCondEndBlock) would make this clearer. This is not a defect in content, order or clipping.
